sentences.text: Ms. Namrata K. Agrawal - advocate for the appellant.

Mr. Anubhav Jain - Government Advocate for the responden
Heard on I.A.No.23666 of 2024, an application for urgent hearing.
For the reasons stated in the application, I.A.No.23666 of 2024 is allowed.
Earlier application has been dismissed on merits vide order dated 20/01/2023.
The case of prosecution is that on 25/03/2018, victim was sexually assaulted by the accused at her house, as a result of which, the victim 2 CRA-6477-2021 committed suicide by handing.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that looking to the statement of Smt. Munni Bai (PW-4),
it is seen that evidence of prosecutrix is not natural.
There was no sign of struggle.
In merg intimation report (Ex.P/9) there was no allegation of rape.
The appellant is in custody since 02/04/2018.
It is further submitted that the final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
He is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering the application for suspension of sentence.
Hence, he prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the application and prays for its rejection.
On perusal of the record, it is seen that that evidence of Smt. Munni Bai (PW-4) is prima facie not convincing as this witness aged about seventeen and half years on the date of incident.
In para - 2 she has stated that accused caught hold of hands of the prosecutrix and dragged her into another room.
Out of fear she went to uncle's house and called her cousin brothers and thereafter they came back to the house.
They saw that accused was hiding beneath the cot and prosecutrix was weeping and his brother slapped the accused and thereafter he ran away.
The prosecutrix said that since wrong has been committed upon her, therefore she would not live any more.
Thereafter she alongwith her brother went to see Jawari function.
There is no DNA report and there was no medical evidence against the accused regarding rape in Postmortem report.
Prosecutrix has not been held 3 CRA-6477-2021 to be minor by the Court and accused has been acquitted from the charges levelled under Section 4 of the POCSO Act.

Considering the over all facts and circumstances of the case and the custody period of the appellant,
and without expressing any conclusive opinion on the merits of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.16972 of 2024 is allowed and it is directed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain under suspension subject to the verification for the fact that the amount of fine has been deposited and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the trial Court/concerned Court on 17.12.2024 and thereafter on such other subsequent dates as may be fixed in that behalf.
List for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
